source_doc: Exercises/Build_an_Interactive_Dashboard.docx > Instructions, Parts 1 to 6 (steps 1 to 20); Part 5 and Part 6 alone, on take08's codespace (Phase 3 test take) (merged with dashboard_20261007_p5_take01/generated.json)

variables.feedback_prompt: In the Period filter, I clicked Last 12 months. The two boxes at the ends of the slider show 57 and 68, which look like month numbers. I expected dates, such as Oct 2024 and Sep 2025.
variables.feedback_prompt_2: I reloaded the page and clicked Last 12 months again. The two boxes at the ends of the Period slider still show 57 and 68 instead of dates.

ide.notes: A test of Part 5 on take08's codespace, where Claude built the dashboard in s7_take06: the window as Part 4 leaves it (the Codespaces page, the IDE with the Explorer, Claude Code's last conversation and the Ports view, the dashboard in front). The README preview a reconnect opens is closed first.

narration.text: Now let's explore the dashboard Claude built. Your dashboard won't look exactly like this one, because Claude makes different choices each time.

steps.notes: Recording resumes here after the off-camera exploration (R70). The runner saves the dashboard still for the opening and recap graphics (R69).

narration.text: At the top are the filters and settings. Below them are six summary tiles. The Stress index tile is a calculated field Claude added: it combines delay, taxi-out time, and cancellations, so it isn't in the raw data. Further down are a map of the airports, and a ranking of the top fifteen.
points: A one-sentence tour, top down, with overview marks on each region (R48 fade marks; doc's run: filters, parameters, KPI tiles, map, ranking).
One calculated field Claude added that isn't in the raw data (e.g. cancellation rate, a prior-year comparison).
If it added outside context, such as known disruptions labelled as outside the data: that's the prompt's "don't limit yourself to just what's in the data" at work.

narration.text: First, a filter. Under Period, I'll click Last 12 months. The period now runs from October 2024 to September 2025, and the map and the ranking update.
points: A filter: a date range or a region (e.g. a preset such as Last 12 months). Announce, act, and say what changed (R23, R24).

narration.text: Next, a parameter. Under Map / ranking metric, I'll open the list,
points: A parameter: the metric, an alert threshold, or the number of airports in the ranking.

narration.text: and choose Avg departure delay. The map and the ranking now show each airport's delay, instead of the stress index.

steps.notes: The dropdown's second click (generated, after p5.14d opens the list).

narration.text: In the ranking, I'll click the top bar, SFB, for Sanford, Florida. The tiles, the map, and the ranking all focus on that one airport. Each click goes to the Python program, which filters the data and redraws the charts.
points: Cross-filtering: click an airport (a bar, bubble or table row) to drill in, and every chart updates.
Why it works, in one sentence: each click goes to the Python program, which filters the data and redraws the charts (the doc's Callbacks in depth).

narration.text: But notice the two boxes at the ends of the Period slider. After I clicked Last 12 months, they read 57 and 68, not dates. Claude can't see the page it built, so we need to tell it.
points: The real defect found while exploring, marked on screen. Earlier runs: the period boxes read 57 and 68 instead of dates; the map zoomed in until it was almost blank (the doc's example).
Pattern: "Notice that <defect>. Claude tested its code, but it can't see the page, so we need to tell it."
With no defect, an improvement in the doc's style instead, e.g. "Add a comparison of taxi-in and taxi-out times."

narration.text: I'll switch back to the codespace tab,

steps.notes: The runner reads the tab's place in the strip from the screen and the edit draws the move and click (switch_tab).

narration.text: and describe the problem in the message box: what I clicked, what I saw, and what I expected. The more precisely we describe a problem, the faster Claude can fix it.

variants.improvement: and describe the change I want in the message box: what I'd like to see, and where. The more precisely we describe a change, the faster Claude can make it.

steps.notes: The prompt text is generated with the defect (variable feedback_prompt), in the doc's pattern: say what you saw, where, and what you expected. Typed at natural speed, not pasted (R67): the edit speeds the typing up or cuts its middle, so the line plays over the finished prompt. The description carries every prompt.

narration.text: I'll click the send arrow.

steps.notes: Send arrow confirmed in take06 (2026-10-07). The busy panel shows 'Queue another message'.

points: Claude can't reproduce a visual problem on its own: it explains its fix and may ask you to check it.
A pkill prompt to restart the dashboard is routine (1x, a visible click).

narration.text: Claude reports that the problem is fixed. I'll switch back to the dashboard tab,

variants.improvement: Claude reports that the change is made. I'll switch back to the dashboard tab,

steps.notes: The runner reads the tab's place in the strip from the screen and the edit draws the move and click (switch_tab).

narration.text: and reload the page to load the new version.
I'll click Last 12 months again. This time, the period shows as dates.
points: Repeat the click that showed the defect, and confirm the fix out loud (R24).
One round is recorded. "Each round of feedback refines the dashboard" (doc) can be said here.

only_if.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('#range input')].filter(i => i.offsetParent); return b.length > 0 && b.every(i => /^\d+$/.test(i.value.trim())); })()

narration.text: The boxes still show numbers, so let's tell Claude again. I'll switch back to the codespace tab,

steps.notes: R70's second round: runs only while the defect still shows after the reload (only_if eval); p5.15j-o follow its decision.

narration.text: and describe what I still see.
I'll click the send arrow.
I'll switch back to the dashboard tab,
and reload the page.
I'll click Last 12 months again.
When you finish exploring, it's good practice to stop the dashboard. I'll switch back to the codespace tab,

steps.notes: The runner reads the tab's place in the strip from the screen and the edit draws the move and click (switch_tab).

only_if.eval: (() => { const b = [...document.querySelectorAll('#range input')].filter(i => i.offsetParent); return !(b.length > 0 && b.every(i => /^\d+$/.test(i.value.trim()))); })()

action.text: I'm done exploring for now; please stop the dashboard.

narration.text: and ask Claude to stop the dashboard. The dashboard is a running program, so it keeps running until something stops it.
I'll click the send arrow.

steps.notes: Send arrow confirmed in take06 (2026-10-07). The busy panel shows 'Queue another message'.

points: "Allow this bash command?" for the command that stops the dashboard: Claude asks before it stops a program. Routine here: click Yes (1x, a visible click).
Claude confirms the dashboard has stopped.

narration.text: In the Ports tab, notice that the dot next to port 8050 is now hollow. That means the dashboard has stopped.

steps.notes: The status icon is codicon-ports-forwarded-with-process-icon (a filled dot) while the app runs; the row's aria-label holds localhost:8050 (take08, 2026-10-07). Measured after Claude stops the app.

points: Read Claude's final report: it lists the new files (doc's run: app.py and assets/style.css).
And side effects, such as a package it installed along the way. The report is where you learn about them.

action.text: Let's wrap up. Write notes about the dashboard in docs/dashboard.md: what it does, how to start it, where its files are, and any decisions we made. Then add a one-line pointer to that file in CLAUDE.md, so you can find the notes in future sessions.

narration.text: Before we finish, I'll ask Claude to wrap up. I'll enter the wrap-up prompt.

steps.notes: Typed at natural speed, not pasted (R67): the edit speeds the typing up or cuts its middle, so the line plays over the finished prompt. The description carries every prompt.

narration.text: The prompt asks Claude to write notes about the dashboard in docs/dashboard.md, and to add a one-line pointer to them in CLAUDE.md. That's our first standing rule at work.
End every working session this way. Claude starts each session with no memory of the last one. It reads CLAUDE.md first, and the pointer leads it to the notes.
I'll click the send arrow.

steps.notes: Send arrow confirmed in take06 (2026-10-07). The busy panel shows 'Queue another message'.

points: Claude wrote the notes to docs/dashboard.md and added the one-line pointer to CLAUDE.md (doc step 18).

action.text: Commit all of my changes to the main branch with a short message that describes what we built, and push them to GitHub.

expect.value: uilt, and push them to GitHub.

narration.text: Now let's save our work to GitHub. I'll enter the commit prompt.

steps.notes: Typed at natural speed, not pasted (R67): the edit speeds the typing up or cuts its middle, so the line plays over the finished prompt. The description carries every prompt.

narration.text: Notice that the prompt names the main branch, which matches our second rule. You can also commit the changes yourself with the Source Control icon on the left edge. I won't do that here, but will instead let Claude handle it.
I'll click the send arrow.

steps.notes: Send arrow confirmed in take06 (2026-10-07). The busy panel shows 'Queue another message'.

points: Claude confirms the work is committed and pushed to GitHub (doc step 20).
The U markers in the Explorer disappear: the files are in the repository now.
Committing means the dashboard survives even if the codespace is deleted; files that live only in a codespace disappear with it.

steps.notes: The autopilot's RISKY list holds `git push`; this step allows it (action.allow): the push goes to the take's own repo, the one the codespace was made from.

generated.defect: After I click Last 12 months, the two boxes at the ends of the Period slider read 57 and 68 (month numbers) where I expected dates such as Oct 2024 and Sep 2025.
generated.notes: Explored off camera on this take's dashboard (explore/: inventory, try_01..04). Interactions, all in the first screen: the Last 12 months preset (a filter), the Map / ranking metric dropdown to Avg departure delay (a parameter, two clicks), the top ranking bar, SFB (cross-filtering: tiles, map ring, chip). The defect meets R70's four tests: (1) visible at once, the boxes sit at the top left; (2) one sentence: clicked Last 12 months, saw 57 and 68, expected dates; (3) one round: Dash 4.4's RangeSlider draws these number boxes by default, and they can be hidden or replaced; (4) shown fixed by clicking Last 12 months again after the reload. The doc's map example does not occur: the map is a fixed U.S. albers projection. A second round (p5.15i-o) runs only if the boxes still read numbers after the reload; p5.16a stops the take if they still do after it (R70: then David decides).
